paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend. Joash does what is right in the eyes of the LORD "all the days of Jehoiada the priest" (2 Chronicles 24:2). Hold onto that line. It tells us his good living had a good man standing next to it the whole time. And I'm not saying that's a bad thing, because I needed a Mother Miller to pick me out of a bin, so I know what help looks like.

But look at what the help produced. Joash "set his heart on repairing the house of the LORD" (2 Chronicles 24:4), and when the Levites did not make haste, he did not just sit there. He called in Jehoiada, built a chest, and sent out a proclamation (2 Chronicles 24:6, 8-9). Then the people rejoiced, gave until the chest was full, and the work got done (2 Chronicles 24:10, 13). A heart set on God's house, plus people who gave gladly, got a whole temple restored.

So here's my question for you, baker. Who is your Jehoiada? Thank God for them, and thank them too. Then ask yourself whether your walk with God would still stand if they weren't beside you, because Jehoiada died at 130 and the passage ends there (2 Chronicles 24:15). Joash's story isn't over yet, and I want you to hold this lesson in your hands before the next one.
